reason: The text begins by stating that the Israelites 'did evil in the sight of the Lord' and were consequently delivered into Midian's hand for seven years, resulting in severe suffering. When the people cry out, God sends a prophet who explicitly tells them their suffering is their fault, saying 'I brought you up from Egypt... but you have not listened to my voice' (וְלֹ֥א שְׁמַעְתֶּ֖ם בְּקוֹלִֽי). The prophet-messenger, functioning as a leader, directly attributes their oppression by the Midianites to their disobedience and evil actions. The causal link between their wrongdoing and their suffering is established clearly at the passage's beginning and reinforced by the prophet's rebuke during their distress.
